questions.problem: A particle moves along a straight line relative to a fixed origin $O$ with acceleration, measured in ${\text{m/s}}^{2},$ given by the function $a(t)=\frac{1}{2}{t}^{4}-3{t}^{3}+t$, where $t$ is the time in seconds. If the particle has velocity $v=-10\,\text{m/s}$ when $t=0\,\text{s}$, calculate the speed of the particle at the moment $t=2\,\text{s}.$
questions.worked_solution:
First, we find $v(t)$ by integrating the acceleration with respect to time:

$$
\begin{aligned}v(t) & =\int a(t)\text{d}t \\  & =\int (\frac{1}{2}{t}^{4}-3{t}^{3}+t)\text{d}t \\  & =\frac{1}{10}{t}^{5}-\frac{3}{4}{t}^{4}+\frac{1}{2}{t}^{2}+C\end{aligned}
$$

To determine $C$, we use the fact that $v(0)=-10.$ Substituting this into the above gives

$$
\begin{aligned}-10 & =\frac{1}{10}(0)^{5}-\frac{3}{4}(0)^{4}+\frac{1}{2}(0)^{2}+C \\ -10 & =0+C \\ C & =-10.\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the velocity $v$ of the particle at time $t$ is $v(t)=\frac{1}{10}{t}^{5}-\frac{3}{4}{t}^{4}+\frac{1}{2}{t}^{2}-10.$

We evaluate the velocity at time $t=2\,\text{s}$:

$$
\begin{aligned}v(2) & =\frac{1}{10}(2)^{5}-\frac{3}{4}(2)^{4}+\frac{1}{2}(2)^{2}-10 \\  & =3.2-12+2-10 \\  & =-16.8\,\text{m/s}\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, since the speed is equal to $|v(t)|,$ we conclude that the speed of the particle is $16.8\,\text{m/s}.$

questions.problem: A particle moves along a straight line relative to a fixed origin $O$ with acceleration, measured in $\text{m}/{\text{s}}^{2},$ given by the function $a(t)=6{t}^{2}-2t-10$, where $t$ is the time in seconds. If the particle has velocity $v=-4\,\text{m}/\text{s}$ when $t=1\,\text{s}$, calculate the speed of the particle at the moment $t=3\,\text{s}.$
questions.worked_solution:
First, we find $v(t)$ by integrating the acceleration with respect to time:

$$
\begin{aligned}v(t) & =\int a(t)\text{d}t \\  & =\int (6{t}^{2}-2t-10)\text{d}t \\  & =2{t}^{3}-{t}^{2}-10t+C\end{aligned}
$$

To determine $C$, we use the fact that $v(1)=-4.$ Substituting this into the above gives

$$
\begin{aligned}-4 & =2(1)^{3}-(1)^{2}-10(1)+C \\ -4 & =2-1-10+C \\ C & =5.\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the velocity $v$ of the particle at time $t$ is $v(t)=2{t}^{3}-{t}^{2}-10t+5.$

We evaluate the velocity at time $t=3\,\text{s}$:

$$
\begin{aligned}v(3) & =2(3)^{3}-(3)^{2}-10(3)+5 \\  & =54-9-30+5 \\  & =20\,\text{m/s}\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, since the speed is equal to $|v(t)|,$ we conclude that the speed of the particle is $20\,\text{m/s}.$

questions.problem: A particle moves along a straight line relative to a fixed origin $O$ with acceleration, measured in $\text{m}/{\text{s}}^{2},$ given by the function $a(t)=2t+{t}^{2}$, where $t$ is the time in seconds. If the particle has velocity $v=\frac{8}{3}\,\text{m}/\text{s}$ when $t=1\,\text{s}$, calculate the velocity of the particle at the moment $t=2\,\text{s}.$
questions.worked_solution:
First, we find $v(t)$ by integrating the acceleration with respect to time:

$$
\begin{aligned}v(t) & =\int a(t)\text{d}t \\  & =\int (2t+{t}^{2})\text{d}t \\  & ={t}^{2}+\frac{{t}^{3}}{3}+C\end{aligned}
$$

To determine $C$, we use the fact that $v(1)=\frac{8}{3}.$ Substituting this into the above gives

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{8}{3} & =(1)^{2}+\frac{(1)^{3}}{3}+C \\ \frac{8}{3} & =1+\frac{1}{3}+C \\ C & =\frac{4}{3}.\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the velocity $v$ of the particle at time $t$ is $v(t)=\frac{4}{3}+{t}^{2}+\frac{{t}^{3}}{3}.$

We evaluate the velocity at time $t=2\,\text{s}$:

$$
\begin{aligned}v(2) & =\frac{4}{3}+(2)^{2}+\frac{(2)^{3}}{3} \\  & =\frac{4}{3}+4+\frac{8}{3} \\  & =8\,\text{m/s}\end{aligned}
$$

questions.problem: A particle moves along a straight line relative to a fixed origin $O$ with acceleration, measured in ${\text{m/s}}^{2},$ given by the function $a(t)=3+8t-3{t}^{2}$, where $t$ is the time in seconds. If the particle has velocity $v=-1\,\text{m/s}$ when $t=0\,\text{s}$, calculate the speed of the particle at the moment $t=2\,\text{s}.$
questions.worked_solution:
First, we find $v(t)$ by integrating the acceleration with respect to time:

$$
\begin{aligned}v(t) & =\int a(t)\text{d}t \\  & =\int (3+8t-3{t}^{2})\text{d}t \\  & =3t+4{t}^{2}-{t}^{3}+C\end{aligned}
$$

To determine $C$, we use the fact that $v(0)=-1.$ Substituting this into the above gives

$$
\begin{aligned}-1 & =3(0)+4(0)^{2}-(0)^{3}+C \\ -1 & =0+C \\ C & =-1.\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the velocity $v$ of the particle at time $t$ is $v(t)=3t+4{t}^{2}-{t}^{3}-1.$

We evaluate the velocity at time $t=2\,\text{s}$:

$$
\begin{aligned}v(2) & =3(2)+4(2)^{2}-(2)^{3}-1 \\  & =6+16-8-1 \\  & =13\,\text{m/s}\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, since the speed is equal to $|v(t)|,$ we conclude that the speed of the particle is $13\,\text{m/s}.$

questions.problem: A particle moves along a straight line relative to a fixed origin $O$ with acceleration, measured in $\text{m}/{\text{s}}^{2},$ given by the function $a(t)=-6{e}^{-2t}$, where $t$ is the time in seconds. If the particle has velocity $v=2\,\text{m}/\text{s}$ when $t=0\,\text{s}$, find the velocity (in $\text{m/s}$)  of the particle at time $t.$
questions.worked_solution:
First, we find $v(t)$ by integrating the acceleration with respect to time:

$$
\begin{aligned}v(t) & =\int a(t)\,\text{d}t \\  & =\int (-6{e}^{-2t})\,\text{d}t \\  & =-6(-\frac{1}{2}{e}^{-2t})+C \\  & =3{e}^{-2t}+C\end{aligned}
$$

To determine $C$, we use the fact that $v(0)=2.$ Substituting this into the above gives

$$
\begin{aligned}2 & =3{e}^{0}+C \\ 2 & =3+C \\ C & =-1.\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, the velocity $v$ of the particle at time $t$ is $v(t)=3{e}^{-2t}-1.$

questions.problem:
A particle moves along a straight line relative to a fixed origin $O$ with acceleration $a(t)=\frac{3}{\sqrt{t+1}},$ where $a(t)$ is measured in ${\text{ft/s}}^{2}$ and $t$ is measured in seconds. Find the speed of the particle at the moment $t=3\,\text{s}$ given that the particle has velocity $v=\frac{1}{2}\,\text{ft/s}$ when $t=0\,\text{s}.$

The speed at the moment $t=3\,\text{s}$ is
{{field-1}} $\,\text{ft/s}.$
questions.worked_solution:
First, we find $v(t)$ by integrating the acceleration with respect to time:

$$
\begin{aligned}v(t) & =\int a(t)\,\text{d}t \\  & =\int \frac{3}{\sqrt{t+1}}\,\text{d}t \\  & =6\sqrt{t+1}+C\end{aligned}
$$

To determine $C$, we use the fact that $v(0)=\frac{1}{2}.$ Substituting this into the above gives

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{1}{2} & =6\sqrt{0+1}+C \\ \frac{1}{2} & =6+C \\ C & =-\frac{11}{2}.\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the velocity $v$ of the particle at time $t$ is $v(t)=6\sqrt{t+1}-\frac{11}{2}.$

We evaluate the velocity at time $t=3\,\text{s}:$

$$
\begin{aligned}v(3) & =6\sqrt{3+1}-\frac{11}{2} \\  & =6(2)-\frac{11}{2} \\  & =\frac{24}{2}-\frac{11}{2} \\  & =\frac{13}{2}\,\text{ft/s}\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, since the speed is equal to $|v(t)|,$ we conclude that the speed of the particle is $\frac{13}{2}\,\text{ft/s}.$

If the particle has a velocity $v=1$ when $t=0\,\text{s}$, find the velocity (in $\text{m/s}$)  of the particle at time $t.$
questions.worked_solution:
First, we find $v(t)$ by integrating the acceleration with respect to time:

$$
\begin{aligned}v(t) & =\int a(t)\,\text{d}t \\  & =\int \frac{1}{(t+1)^{2}}\,\text{d}t \\  & =-\frac{1}{t+1}+C\end{aligned}
$$

To determine $C$, we use the fact that $v(0)=1.$ Substituting this into the above gives

$$
\begin{aligned}1 & =-\frac{1}{0+1}+C \\ 1 & =-1+C \\ C & =2.\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, the velocity $v$ of the particle at time $t$ is $v(t)=-\frac{1}{t+1}+2.$

A particle moves along a straight line relative to a fixed origin $O$ with acceleration $a(t)=5{e}^{t},$ where $a(t)$ is measured in ${\text{m/s}}^{2}$ and $t$ is measured in seconds. Find the speed of the particle at the moment $t=\operatorname{ln}⁡2\,\text{s}$ given that the particle has velocity $v=\frac{1}{2}\,\text{m/s}$ when $t=0\,\text{s}.$

The speed at the moment $t=\operatorname{ln}⁡2\,\text{s}$ is
{{field-1}} $\,\text{m/s}.$
questions.worked_solution:
First, we find $v(t)$ by integrating the acceleration with respect to time:

$$
\begin{aligned}v(t) & =\int a(t)\,\text{d}t \\  & =\int 5{e}^{t}\,\text{d}t \\  & =5{e}^{t}+C\end{aligned}
$$

To determine $C$, we use the fact that $v(0)=\frac{1}{2}.$ Substituting this into the above gives

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{1}{2} & =5{e}^{0}+C \\ \frac{1}{2} & =5+C \\ C & =-\frac{9}{2}.\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the velocity $v$ of the particle at time $t$ is $v(t)=5{e}^{t}-\frac{9}{2}.$

We evaluate the velocity at time $t=\operatorname{ln}⁡2\,\text{s}:$

$$
\begin{aligned}v(\operatorname{ln}⁡2) & =5{e}^{\operatorname{ln}⁡2}-\frac{9}{2} \\  & =5(2)-\frac{9}{2} \\  & =\frac{20}{2}-\frac{9}{2} \\  & =\frac{11}{2}\,\text{m/s}\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, since the speed is equal to $|v(t)|,$ we conclude that the speed of the particle is $\frac{11}{2}\,\text{m/s}.$

If the particle has velocity $v=2\,\textrm m / \textrm s$ when $t=0 \,\textrm s,$ calculate the velocity (in $\textrm m / \textrm s$) of the particle at time $t.$
canonical_examples.worked_solution:
First, we find $v(t)$ by integrating the acceleration with respect to time:

$$
\begin{aligned}v(t) & =\int a(t)\text{d}t \\  & =\int (4{t}^{2}-3{t}^{3})\text{d}t \\  & =\frac{4}{3}{t}^{3}-\frac{3}{4}{t}^{4}+C\end{aligned}
$$

To determine $C,$ we use the fact that $v(0) = 2.$ Substituting this into the above gives

$$
\begin{aligned}2 & =\frac{4}{3}(0)^{3}-\frac{3}{4}(0)^{4}+C \\ C & =2.\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the velocity $v$ of the particle at time $t$ is $v(t) = \dfrac{4}{3}t^3 -\dfrac{3}{4}t^4 + 2.$

canonical_examples.problem: A particle moves along a straight line relative to a fixed origin $O$ with acceleration, measured in $\textrm m / \textrm s^2,$ given by the function $a(t) =2e^{-t}+6t^2$, where $t$ is the time in seconds. If the particle has velocity $v=-4 \,\textrm m / \textrm s$ when $t=0 \,\textrm s,$ calculate the speed of the particle at the moment  $t=1\,\textrm{s}.$
canonical_examples.worked_solution:
First, we find $v(t)$ by integrating the acceleration with respect to time:

$$
\begin{aligned}v(t) & =\int a(t)\text{d}t \\  & =\int (2{e}^{-t}+6{t}^{2})\text{d}t \\  & =2(-{e}^{-t})+\frac{6}{3}{t}^{3}+C \\  & =-2{e}^{-t}+2{t}^{3}+C\end{aligned}
$$

To determine $C$, we use the fact that $v(0) = -4.$ Substituting this into the above gives

$$
\begin{aligned}-4 & =-2{e}^{-0}+2\cdot {0}^{3}+C \\ -4 & =-2+0+C \\ C & =-2.\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the velocity $v$ of the particle at time $t$ is $v(t) = -2  e^{-t}+ 2t^3 -2.$

We evaluate the velocity at time $t=1\,\textrm{s}\mathbin{:}$

$$
\begin{aligned}v(1) & =-2{e}^{-1}+2(1)^{3}-2 \\  & =-2{e}^{-1}+2-2 \\  & =-\frac{2}{e}\,\text{m/s}\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, since the speed is equal to $|v(t)|,$ we conclude that the speed of the particle is $\dfrac 2 e\,\textrm{m/s}.$
